questions.question: You receive one extraordinary power. What would you most want to do with it?

answers.text: Become one formidable champion who can take on anyone.
Lead a huge force whose members strengthen one another.
Combine magical abilities into unexpected results.
Stop threats and decide what others can do.

questions.question: Rank what you would prioritize before a difficult battle.

answers.text: Strike early and keep up pressure.
Build reliable resources and become stronger over time.
Prepare responses to an opponent’s plans.
Assemble a plan with a spectacular payoff.

questions.question: How satisfying is it to watch something you built gradually grow stronger?
A favorite ally has been defeated. What would feel most satisfying?

answers.text: Bring them back to fight again.
Get rewarded because they were defeated.
Protect the rest of my team and adjust.
Attack immediately to avenge them.

questions.question: Put these projects in order from most interesting to least interesting.

answers.text: Build a team of creatures that becomes powerful together.
Create lasting magical effects that improve everything you do.
Connect inventions that give each other new abilities.
Expand your territory to produce more resources over time.

questions.question: How much do you enjoy having opportunities to interfere with an opponent’s plans?
You have a limited amount of power to spend this turn. Which use appeals most?

answers.text: Use it all now for one impactful move.
Spend it on several improvements that add up later.
Keep some in reserve in case something goes wrong.
Invest in a specific payoff that could become amazing later.

questions.question: Rank these endings from most satisfying to least satisfying.

answers.text: An army overwhelms the battlefield.
One legendary champion lands the final hit.
A clever combination wins suddenly.
I outlast everyone until they have no answers.

questions.question: You can give your allies one unusual ability. Which do you choose?

answers.text: Keep gaining permanent strength.
Disappear and return to reuse special abilities.
Create extra allies as you play.
Reward me for casting spells in succession.

questions.question: How much would you enjoy keeping track of several abilities that trigger and interact with one another?
Someone seems impossible to beat in a fair fight. What would you try?

answers.text: Use their best resource against them.
Take apart the resources supporting their strategy.
Convince another player to help me.
Pursue an unusual objective that bypasses combat.

questions.question: If you could win without attacking with creatures, how would you want to?

answers.text: Steal away their life while restoring mine.
Blast them with spells and direct damage.
Empty their library so they cannot draw a card.
Fulfill an unusual condition that says I win.

questions.question: How willing would you be to risk your current progress for a chance at a much bigger payoff?
Pick up to two experiences you would love to have in a game.

answers.text: Feel powerful through creatures and combat.
Build a system that generates benefits turn after turn.
Predict and stop an opponent’s important move.
Pull off an unexpected combination.

questions.question: You are losing, but you have enough resources for one meaningful move. What do you prioritize?

answers.text: Make the strongest move possible right now to turn things around.
Recover what you lost and rebuild from there.
Keep your options open to stop the next dangerous move.
Attempt an unlikely plan with a chance to win outright.

questions.question: Rank the armies you would most like to lead.

answers.text: One unstoppable hero
Several enormous monsters
Many small allies
A team that upgrades together

questions.question: How appealing is turning one creature into an almost unstoppable champion?
How appealing is controlling a huge army of smaller creatures?
Your group has survived a difficult fight. Which upgrade feels most rewarding?

answers.text: Make each survivor individually stronger.
Create reinforcements to replace losses.
Give everyone a bonus when teammates work together.
Make it much harder for your favorite ally to be defeated.

questions.question: Which two themes would you actually want to see in your deck?

answers.text: Dragons and enormous beasts.
Spirits, ghosts, and creatures returning from death.
Constructs, robots, and inventions.
Wizards with weird magical abilities.

questions.question: You unexpectedly get enough resources for something expensive. What do you do?

answers.text: Summon something huge that can attack.
Add several more creatures to the battlefield.
Give your main fighter a permanent upgrade.
Build an engine that keeps paying you back.

questions.question: How satisfying would it be if every new member of your team strengthened the others?
How enjoyable would managing a crowded battlefield with many creatures and abilities be?
One of your actions can trigger a reward every turn. What reward do you want?

answers.text: Permanently strengthen a creature.
Create a fresh ally.
Draw more options to choose from.
Deal a little damage to each opponent.

questions.question: How appealing is keeping track of +1/+1 counters and watching individual creatures develop?
Rank these ways of using creatures more than once.

answers.text: Bring them back after they die
Sacrifice them for rewards
Exile and return them to reuse abilities
Make copies of them

questions.question: How satisfying is having your own creatures die because it helps your strategy?
You discover a workshop with four different crafts. What would you learn?

answers.text: Build objects whose abilities depend on other objects.
Create magic that stays in place and changes the rules.
Chain spells together for growing effects.
Make creatures that produce useful effects when they arrive.

questions.question: How much would you enjoy several little effects triggering one after another?
Pick up to two resources you would be most excited to have in abundance.

answers.text: Extra life and recovery
More mana and lands
More cards to choose from
More creatures

questions.question: Your carefully built strategy falls apart halfway through a game. What would you prefer?

answers.text: Get my key pieces back from the graveyard.
Have plenty of backup cards available.
Make opponents suffer for destroying my things.
Switch to a different plan with the resources I have.

questions.question: How appealing is gaining life repeatedly while your other abilities do their jobs?
Rank these setbacks from MOST frustrating to LEAST frustrating.

answers.text: Losing the creatures I spent turns developing.
Running out of cards and useful choices.
Falling far behind in the first few turns.
Never finding the pieces my strategy depends on.

questions.question: If you could reuse the same type of resource again and again, which would be most interesting?

answers.text: Spells I have already cast.
Creatures that were defeated.
Abilities on objects and artifacts.
Abilities of creatures that temporarily leave and return.

questions.question: How appealing is having a deck that behaves like a machine, with many interconnected pieces?
Rank these victories from most satisfying to least satisfying.

answers.text: Win through combat attacks.
Win by casting damaging magic directly.
Win by repeatedly draining life.
Win by emptying an opponent’s library.

questions.question: How satisfying is slowly wearing opponents down instead of winning all at once?
An opponent has a valuable permanent. What would you rather do?

answers.text: Steal and use it
Destroy it
Temporarily stop it from working
Ignore it and improve my own board

questions.question: How appealing is making opponents discard cards or lose access to options?
Which two surprising victory stories would you most want to experience?

answers.text: A series of effects combine into a winning loop.
I meet an unusual requirement that wins immediately.
My commander becomes the biggest threat on the table.
An enormous coordinated attack finishes everyone.

questions.question: Attacking directly is not working. What sounds like the best alternate plan?

answers.text: Keep gathering resources until my board is stronger.
Make every action slowly drain the opponent’s life.
Chase a special win condition that ignores combat.
Destroy their resources until defending is impossible.

questions.question: How appealing is a card that lets you win by meeting a strange, specific condition?
Rank ways you would prefer to manage an opposing threat.

answers.text: Prevent it before it happens
Remove it after it appears
Steal it
Persuade another player to handle it

questions.question: What kind of action would you most enjoy punishing?

answers.text: An opponent attacking me.
An opponent casting too many spells.
An opponent drawing lots of cards.
An opponent building a large army.

questions.question: How fun would it be to play cards borrowed or stolen from your opponents?
Rank what you care about most in a win.

answers.text: Winning quickly
Winning reliably
Winning through a clever sequence
Winning after surviving a long struggle

questions.question: How comfortable are you taking turns with many separate decisions and triggered abilities?
You can choose one reward for completing a difficult task. Which would you take?

answers.text: A modest reward I know I will receive.
A much larger reward that only works if my plan succeeds.
A flexible reward I can choose later once I know more.
An immediate reward that lets me take action again.

questions.question: How frustrating would it be if your deck took several turns to get started?
Pick the two moments you would most look forward to.

answers.text: Landing a decisive attack.
Getting a complicated system to work.
Responding perfectly to an opponent’s move.
Discovering a strange combination.

questions.question: A player offers a temporary alliance. What would you do?

answers.text: Accept if we share an immediate goal.
Negotiate exactly what each of us gets.
Decline; I want to focus on my own plan.
Agree only if it stops the strongest player.

questions.question: How important is it to recover quickly after losing your main strategy?
Rank the qualities that make a deck appealing to you.

answers.text: A straightforward strategy that is easy to operate.
Lots of technical choices and intricate decisions.
Wild swings and unpredictable outcomes.
Reliable plans with opportunities to adapt.

questions.question: What kind of deck would be most satisfying to improve at over time?

answers.text: One that does the same job reliably, and I learn to execute it well.
One that can switch between several plans.
One with surprising and unpredictable outcomes.
One where precise timing changes everything.

questions.question: How appealing is carefully timing plays around what your opponents are doing?
At a multiplayer table, what role sounds most fun?

answers.text: Being the obvious threat everyone must answer.
Staying unnoticed until my plan comes together.
Negotiating and making temporary allies.
Keeping dangerous opponents in check.

questions.question: How appealing is a strategy that sometimes does very little before one huge payoff?
How appealing is a deck whose best plays depend on what your opponents have?
questions.left: I want my own game plan

questions.question: How much would you enjoy making many small decisions each turn rather than one or two big decisions?
Which part of a difficult game would frustrate you most?

answers.text: My creatures feel too weak to matter
I keep losing everything I build
I have too many interactions to remember
I spend too long waiting to do anything
